notes.account: The opening, headed only Posons, records three definitions under (13). In the E_2 definition the first Sigma visibly carries subscript 1. The inclusion diagram below places E_2 under Sigma_2^+. Both source forms are retained.

The source calls (14) a diagram of inclusions of closed parts of X and states that the three squares are cartésiens et cocartésiens. Ten live arrows point upward through the four levels. Below E_1 is an abandoned arrow crossed by a zigzag, ending at an uncertain rounded sign. The NB supplies additional intersection and ring-marked inclusion expressions; its written negative superscript in the E_2 intersection is preserved.

An unnumbered display gives one intersection and one union. The following prose announces the two analogous relations and (15) contains the two remaining rows. Corrections survive in the first row and at the X in the second. The right-hand union term has the visible index 22. The lower left relation has three bars beneath the written reference (13). These source comparisons prompted closer viewing; they were not used to alter the ink.

The three rows of (16) end in crossed equalities and slashed empty-set signs. The source then asks to establish the last relation with the above-line word read first as Prouvons and calls the others “les deux premières étant évidentes”. The word’s middle remains uncertain, and its long curved line attaches it to the sentence initial.

The final paragraph records an attempted argument for the last relation, beginning with the empty-set equation for Sigma_12. It goes on to the two empty E terms, names Pi_1 and Pi_2 as deux partitions de X en des parties non vides, and ends with two complement expressions. There are an uncertain verb correction and two cancelled formula starts. The page contains no conclusion beyond the bottom display. This is an account of the source argument; no independent proof is asserted.

No date, title, or separate author page number is visible. A lighter pencil 33 appears at the bottom left and is retained as an archive-number comment. Formula labels (13), (14), (15), and (16) are written at the left of their respective items.

The handwriting comparisons used in reading were the single-stroke 1 versus hooked 2 indices; the three separately visible bars below (13); the straight-legged Pi form; the independent vertical strokes in the resolved cancelled plus signs; and the steeper earlier set separator versus the shallow final stroke. No expected formula supplied a missing index, letter ending, or older glyph.

check_events_explanation: No proof check, re-proof, formal computation, or mathematical certificate was performed. Source-to-source mathematical comparisons were reading cues only and are recorded in the findings and notes.

workflow_feedback.whole_and_halves: Whole image viewed once for layout; each provided half viewed once and read line by line. All agreed prose and glyphs were read from the image, including labels and the marginal note.
workflow_feedback.crops: Fifteen coherent tight crops were made once each from the original whole image, enlarged to 3000 px width with LANCZOS after autocontrast and sharpened. No locus was cropped a second time. No rotation was needed for the visible writing.
workflow_feedback.clipping: No target mark was clipped. Some contextual material at crop boundaries is partial; the targets include their accents, descenders, and terminal strokes. The last two crops include the existing lower paper edge.
workflow_feedback.saving_order: The complete reading.tex was saved before return.json was composed. A later textual consistency pass removed an unsupported marginal comma from reading.tex and recorded the H punctuation difference; no further image view or crop occurred.
workflow_feedback.isolation: Only the assigned page, its supplied witnesses/context, notation-before-scan034, conventions, and crop script were inspected. No other reader or page work was opened.
workflow_feedback.prohibitions: No OCR, recognition software, PDF text layer, external research, or compilation was used.
